hypotheses.statement: Moving 100% of packaging to Supplier B saves 3.0 EUR M per year (procurement's case, management belief)
hypotheses.implication: The proposal's headline saving cannot be approved as stated; the real gross saving is 2.87 EUR M a year before switching cost and stoppage risk

hypotheses.statement: The 12% price reduction applies to the full 25 EUR M packaging spend
hypotheses.implication: The saving base is 23.9 EUR M, not 25 EUR M

hypotheses.statement: Single-sourcing on Supplier B's single plant creates a continuity risk as large as the extra saving the full move brings
hypotheses.implication: The decision is a risk trade-off, not a pure price decision; a second source is worth keeping
hypotheses.rationale: Based on two historical stoppages; small sample

hypotheses.statement: A 70/30 split between Supplier B and the incumbent captures most of the saving at lower risk and is the best risk-adjusted option
hypotheses.implication: Recommend the 70/30 split instead of the 100% move
hypotheses.rationale: The full move earns 2.93 EUR M more over three years before risk; that advantage holds only if Supplier B has at most one stoppage of 14 days or less in 2026-2028. Two stoppages, as in the last three years, reverse it.

hypotheses.statement: Rush freight is an incumbent performance problem that would disappear by moving volume to Supplier B
hypotheses.implication: Rush freight (1.1 EUR M) must be attacked through our own demand forecasting, not supplier choice

hypotheses.statement: The incumbent could backstop Supplier B quickly enough in a stoppage if all volume moved to Supplier B
hypotheses.implication: After a full move, a 9-14 day stoppage would be largely uncovered: the incumbent covers at most 60% and only at two weeks' notice
